[standards/application/kafka-management/STD-APP-KMGMT-001-topic-browser-access.md#executive-summary]

## Executive Summary

This standard defines **mandatory** requirements for developer access to Lenses.io Topic Browser for Kafka topic inspection, debugging, and message analysis. It ensures developers have consistent, secure, and compliant access to view Kafka messages while maintaining PHI/PII protection through data masking policies.
page_texts.3:
[standards/application/kafka-management/STD-APP-KMGMT-001-topic-browser-access.md#key-requirements]

### Key Requirements

- **Topic Discovery**: Search and filter topics by name, tags, and business unit scope
- **Message Browsing**: Live and historical message inspection with filtering capabilities
- **Data Masking**: Automatic PHI/PII masking for all developer access (mandatory)
- **Serialization Support**: Avro, JSON, Protobuf, and String deserialization
- **Access Control**: RBAC-based topic access scoped by business unit
- **Performance Limits**: Rate limiting (100 messages/5 minutes) to prevent cluster impact
page_texts.4:
[standards/application/kafka-management/STD-APP-KMGMT-001-topic-browser-access.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

Topic Browser access is essential for:
- Rapid debugging of event-driven applications
- Message format validation during development
- Integration testing and troubleshooting
- Reducing mean time to resolution (MTTR) for production issues
- Enabling self-service developer productivity
page_texts.5:
[standards/application/kafka-management/STD-APP-KMGMT-001-topic-browser-access.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

**Mandatory** - All developers working with Kafka must have Topic Browser access configured according to this standard.

### 1.1 Purpose

This standard defines mandatory requirements for developer access to Lenses.io Topic Browser, including topic discovery, message inspection, filtering, and data masking policies per [ADR-IFR-008](../../../decisions/infrastructure/ADR-IFR-008-kafka-management-platform-selection.md).
page_texts.9:
[standards/application/kafka-management/STD-APP-KMGMT-001-topic-browser-access.md#12-scope]

### 1.2 Scope

**In Scope**:
- Topic discovery and search functionality
- Message browsing (live and historical)
- Message filtering (by key, value, headers, timestamp)
- Message deserialization (Avro, JSON, Protobuf, String)
- Data masking for PHI/PII topics
- Topic metadata viewing (schema, partition count, retention)
- Developer training and documentation

**Out of Scope**:
- Topic creation/modification (see STD-INFRA-INT-002)
- LSQL query execution (see STD-APP-KMGMT-002)
- Consumer group management (see application standards)
- Production unmasked access (see STD-INFRA-KMGMT-010)

#### REQ-APP-001-001: Topic Discovery and Search

**Status**: Mandatory
**Rationale**: Enable developers to find relevant topics efficiently

**Discovery Methods**:
1. **Topic List View**: All topics developer has access to (scoped by business unit)
2. **Search by Name**: Filter topics by prefix/substring (e.g., `medicaid.*`)
3. **Search by Tag**: Filter by topic tags (e.g., `data-classification: sensitive`)
4. **Favorites**: Bookmark frequently accessed topics
5. **Recent Topics**: View last 10 topics accessed by user

**Access Scoping** (from STD-INFRA-KMGMT-003):
- Developer role: Topics matching `{business-unit}.*` pattern only
- Production Developer role: Production topics (read-only) with data masking
- Platform Admin role: All topics

**Implementation**:

```yaml
  scope.by.business.unit: true

  favorites.enabled: true
  recent.topics.count: 10
```

#### REQ-APP-001-002: Message Browsing (Live Mode)

**Status**: Mandatory
**Rationale**: Real-time message inspection for debugging

**Live Mode Features**:
- Tail topic (subscribe to new messages as they arrive)
- Display message key, value, headers, timestamp, partition, offset
- Auto-refresh every 2 seconds (configurable)
- Pause/resume live stream
- Maximum 100 messages displayed (rolling window)
- Export messages to JSON/CSV (max 1000 messages)

**Use Cases**:
- Verify messages publishing correctly after deployment
- Debug message format issues
- Monitor event flow during integration testing

```javascript
};
```

#### REQ-APP-001-004: Message Deserialization

**Status**: Mandatory
**Rationale**: Display messages in human-readable format

**Supported Formats**:
- **Avro**: Automatically detect schema from Glue Schema Registry
- **JSON**: Pretty-print with syntax highlighting
- **Protobuf**: Deserialize using schema (if available)
- **String**: Display as UTF-8 text
- **Binary**: Display hex dump (with ASCII preview)

**Auto-Detection**: Lenses.io attempts to detect format based on:
1. Schema Registry (if topic uses schema)
2. Content-Type header (if present)
3. Heuristic analysis (JSON braces, Avro magic bytes)

**Fallback**: Display as string if format unknown

**Implementation**:
```yaml
# Placeholder: Deserialization configuration
lenses.topics.deserialization:
  formats: ["avro", "json", "protobuf", "string", "binary"]
  schema.registry.enabled: true
  auto.detect.enabled: true
  # TODO: Add format detection logic
  # TODO: Add custom deserializers
```

#### REQ-APP-001-005: Message Filtering

**Status**: Mandatory
**Rationale**: Focus on relevant messages during debugging

**Filter Types**:
1. **By Message Key**: Filter messages where key matches pattern (regex supported)
2. **By Message Value**: Filter JSON messages where field matches value (e.g., `$.status == "FAILED"`)
3. **By Header**: Filter messages with specific header key/value
4. **By Partition**: Show messages from specific partition only
5. **By Timestamp**: Messages within time range (ISO 8601 format)

**Filter Combinations**: Support AND/OR logic for multiple filters

```json
    {"type": "header", "key": "correlation-id", "value": "abc-123"}
  ],

}
```

#### REQ-APP-001-006: Data Masking Integration

**Status**: Mandatory
**Rationale**: Protect PHI/PII per STD-INFRA-KMGMT-010

**Masking Behavior**:
- **Developer Role**: All PHI/PII fields masked when browsing sensitive topics
- **Production Developer Role**: All production topic data masked (including non-PHI)
- **Platform Admin Role**: Unmasked access (audit logged)

**Masked Display**:
- Masked fields show transformation (e.g., `ssn: "XXX-XX-1234"`)
- Visual indicator: 🔒 icon next to masked fields

### 2.2 Prohibited Practices

The following practices are **explicitly prohibited** when using Topic Browser:

1. **Disabling Data Masking**
   - Developers must NOT attempt to bypass or disable data masking on PHI/PII topics
   - Viewing unmasked PHI/PII without proper authorization violates HIPAA and organizational policies
   - Request proper authorization through STD-INFRA-KMGMT-010 exception process if unmasked access required

2. **Bulk Message Export Without Rate Limiting**
   - Exporting more than 1,000 messages at once is prohibited
   - Mass exports can overload Kafka brokers and impact production workloads
   - For bulk analysis, use approved data pipeline tools (see STD-APP-INT-005)

3. **Sharing Topic Browser Screenshots Containing PHI/PII**
   - Screenshots must NOT be shared in public channels (Slack, Teams, email) if they contain PHI/PII
   - Even masked data should be handled carefully to avoid re-identification risks
   - Use sanitized test data for documentation and training materials

4. **Using Topic Browser as Production Monitoring Tool**
   - Topic Browser is for development/debugging only, not continuous monitoring
   - Production monitoring requires proper observability tools (see STD-IFR-MON-001)
   - Continuous browsing creates unnecessary load on Kafka clusters

5. **Providing Topic Browser Access to Non-Developers**
   - Access limited to developers with valid business need
   - Business analysts and QA personnel should use approved BI tools or test environments
   - Platform Admin role required for production cluster access

6. **Bypassing Access Controls via Direct Kafka API**
   - All topic access must go through Lenses.io (enforces RBAC and data masking)
   - Direct Kafka consumer clients bypass security controls
   - Exception: Application consumers with approved service accounts (see STD-APP-EVT-001)

[standards/application/kafka-management/STD-APP-KMGMT-001-topic-browser-access.md#when-to-request-an-exception]

#### When to Request an Exception

Exceptions may be granted for:
- **Unmasked PHI/PII Access**: Production debugging requiring unmasked data (temporary only)
- **Bulk Export Limits**: Data migration or analysis requiring >1,000 messages
- **Cross-Business-Unit Access**: Temporary access to topics outside developer's business unit
- **Alternative Access Methods**: Valid technical reason to use direct Kafka API (e.g., performance testing)
page_texts.26:
[standards/application/kafka-management/STD-APP-KMGMT-001-topic-browser-access.md#exception-request-procedure]

#### Exception Request Procedure

1. **Submit ServiceNow Request**:
   - Category: "Kafka Topic Browser Access Exception"
   - Include: Business justification, duration needed, data classification, alternative approaches considered

2. **Provide Justification**:
   - Explain why standard approach insufficient
   - Document risk assessment and mitigation plan
   - Specify exact scope of exception (topics, time period)

3. **Technical Review**:
   - Platform Engineering reviews technical feasibility
   - Security reviews compliance and risk implications
   - Data Privacy reviews PHI/PII access requests

4. **Approval Authority**:
   - **Temporary (<30 days)**: Platform Engineering Manager + Security Manager
   - **Extended (30-90 days)**: Chief Architect + CISO
   - **Permanent**: Architecture Review Board + Legal (rare, requires ADR)

[standards/application/kafka-management/STD-APP-KMGMT-001-topic-browser-access.md#32-architecture-constraints]

### 3.2 Architecture Constraints

**Topic Browser Architecture**:
- Topic Browser runs as web application within Lenses.io platform
- All queries proxied through Lenses.io backend (never direct Kafka access)
- Data masking applied at query time before rendering
- WebSocket streaming for live mode (HTTP polling fallback)
- Message caching limited to browser session (no persistent storage)

**Performance Constraints**:
- Maximum 100 concurrent Topic Browser sessions per cluster
- Rate limit: 100 messages per 5 minutes per developer
- Historical searches limited to 10,000 messages
- Export operations queued (max 5 concurrent exports per cluster)

**Security Constraints**:
- All topic access enforced via Lenses RBAC (maps to Okta groups)
- PHI/PII topics require data masking (no exceptions for Developer role)
- Audit logs for all message views (retention: 90 days)
- Session timeout: 2 hours of inactivity

```yaml
lenses:
  security:
    authentication:
      method: "SAML"

    enabled: true
    default-policy: "mask-pii-phi"
    policies:

          - "ssn"

          - "phone_number"

    schema-registry:
      type: "aws-glue"
      auto-register: false
```

[standards/application/kafka-management/STD-APP-KMGMT-001-topic-browser-access.md#issue-1-no-messages-visible-in-topic]

#### Issue 1: No Messages Visible in Topic

**Symptoms**: Topic browse shows "No messages found"

**Resolution**:
1. Verify topic has messages: Check topic metrics (message count)
2. Check retention policy: Messages may have expired
3. Verify partition offset: Try different partition or offset range
4. Check RBAC permissions: User may not have access to topic
page_texts.45:
[standards/application/kafka-management/STD-APP-KMGMT-001-topic-browser-access.md#issue-2-deserialization-error]

#### Issue 2: Deserialization Error

**Symptoms**: Message value shows "Deserialization failed"

**Resolution**:
1. Check schema registry: Verify schema exists for topic
2. Verify schema format: Avro, JSON, Protobuf
3. Check schema version: Topic may use different schema version
4. Fallback to "View as String" mode (raw message)
page_texts.46:
[standards/application/kafka-management/STD-APP-KMGMT-001-topic-browser-access.md#issue-3-performance-degradation-slow-loading]

#### Issue 3: Performance Degradation (Slow Loading)

**Symptoms**: Topic browser takes >10 seconds to load messages

**Resolution**:
1. Reduce time range: Search smaller time window (1h instead of 7d)
2. Reduce page size: Fetch 25 messages instead of 50
3. Check cluster health: Broker CPU/memory usage
4. Check network latency: Lenses.io to MSK connectivity

[standards/application/kafka-management/STD-APP-KMGMT-001-topic-browser-access.md#46-documentation-requirements]

### 4.6 Documentation Requirements

The following documentation must be maintained for Topic Browser compliance:

**1. Access Control Documentation**
- RBAC role definitions and mappings (Developer, ProductionDeveloper)
- Business unit topic scoping rules
- Okta group assignments
- Access request procedures
- Approved exceptions list

**2. Data Masking Documentation**
- PHI/PII field inventory (per topic)
- Masking policy definitions (regex patterns)
- Masking policy assignment (topics → policies)
- Exception approval records (unmasked access)
- Annual masking policy review log

**3. Configuration Documentation**
- Lenses.io platform configuration (YAML)
- Rate limiting thresholds and enforcement
- Session timeout settings
- Deserialization format support
- Schema registry integration

**4. Developer Training Materials**
- Quick start guide (with screenshots)
- Video tutorials (< 5 minutes each)
- Common troubleshooting scenarios
- Office hours schedule and Q&A archive
- FAQ document

**5. Operational Runbook**
- Topic Browser monitoring dashboard
- Performance metrics (latency, throughput, errors)
- Incident response procedures
- Escalation contacts
- Maintenance windows

**6. Compliance Documentation**
- Validation checklist results
- Security testing reports
- Performance benchmarks
- Audit log retention policy
- Exception tracking dashboard

All documentation must be:
- Stored in Confluence workspace (Enterprise Architecture / Kafka Management)
- Version controlled (track major configuration changes)
- Reviewed quarterly by Platform Engineering
- Updated within 10 business days of configuration changes

### 5.3 Governance Oversight

**Standards Owner**: Platform Engineering Team
- Responsible for maintaining and evolving this Topic Browser access standard
- Reviews and approves minor updates to access policies and rate limits
- Conducts quarterly standard effectiveness reviews
- Provides clarifications and interpretations to developers

**Compliance Manager**: Security & Compliance Office
- Monitors organizational compliance with Topic Browser access controls
- Tracks compliance metrics (access violations, masking bypasses, rate limit breaches)
- Conducts monthly random audits of Topic Browser usage and audit logs
- Escalates systemic non-compliance issues to Architecture Review Board

**Governance Body**: Architecture Review Board (ARB)
- Provides oversight and policy direction for Kafka management standards
- Approves major exceptions requiring unmasked PHI/PII access
- Reviews standard compliance metrics quarterly
- Approves major standard revisions and new access patterns

**Subject Matter Experts**: Developer Experience & Data Privacy Teams
- Provides technical guidance on Topic Browser features and best practices
- Supports developers with troubleshooting and optimization
- Reviews data masking policies for accuracy and completeness
- Participates in standard reviews and usability improvements

**Review Frequency**: This standard shall be reviewed:
- Monthly: Compliance metrics and exception tracking by Compliance Manager
- Quarterly: Technical accuracy and usability review by SMEs and Standards Owner
- Annually: Comprehensive effectiveness review by ARB including developer feedback

**Contact Information**:
- Platform Engineering: kafka-support@company.com
- Security & Compliance: compliance@company.com
- ARB Exception Requests: arb-requests@company.com
- Data Privacy Questions: data-privacy@company.com
